The "remember me" checkbox is ignored. Every sign-in lasts a month. Sessions should last 24 hours without it and 30 days with it. Sign-out must end only that specific session. Other devices and accounts remain unaffected.

I need to carefully analyze the bugs before fixing them. Existing rate-limit tests must remain intact.

The bug causes rate limits to leak across accounts. One address triggering too many sign-in attempts or password resets blocks every other account. The fix must isolate limits per account by address, ignoring letter case.

The root cause is that both sign-in and password-reset requests use the same ANONYMOUS_ORG sentinel key. This forces every user into a single shared bucket instead of one per address. The rate limiter itself may be correct; it simply needs to key by email rather than the anonymous organization. I also noticed that both the login action and the auth service appear to call consumeRateLimit, which could mean attempts are being double-charged.

Double rate-limit consumption may be intentional for the contract. I will check the session and login schemas, password-reset email rendering, and destroySession comments to find constraints. A new bug is that sign-out ends every user's session.

`destroySession` calls `purgeExpiredSessions`, which deletes every session older than now. That is why sign-out revokes all sessions. The logout action passes a token to `destroySession`, but the function lacks the session ID that `revokeSession` needs. Signing out should only end the current session and leave other devices signed in.

`destroySession` should delete only the session matching the provided token hash, and silently ignore unknown or already-ended sessions. The `purgeExpiredSessions` logic is also flawed: it deletes every row older than `now`, but since cookies are re-issued on every sign-in, anything predating the sweep is stale by definition. I need to check whether this function is actually used by a cron job.

I will change `purgeExpiredSessions` to delete only sessions where `expiresAt < now`. This fixes housekeeping and prevents `destroySession` from revoking every session. I need a repository method that revokes by token hash or finds the matching session ID.

Checking cron jobs for sessions and how the email schema lowercases values.

SQLite equality is case-sensitive by default. The email lookup must use lower() or COLLATE NOCASE to match mixed-case stored addresses.

Password-reset links expire after one minute instead of sixty. The token lookup ignores usedAt, so expired links remain valid. After a password reset, existing sessions stay active and other accounts are unaffected. Requesting a second reset link leaves the first one working.

New reset links should retire every earlier unused link for that account. Rate limiting is global instead of per-email. Rate-limit buckets key by orgId and bucketKey, so using email as the orgId would create per-email isolation. The login action currently uses ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID. Sign-in throttling must not block password resets. The reset confirmation step should not consume the reset request bucket. It may need its own rate limit or no limit at all.

The shared anonymous bucket is the real problem. One address exhausting its limit blocks resets for everyone. The request action consumes the rate-limit token before the service function does, so each reset request costs two tokens.

The action layer consumes the rate-limit token first. When the bucket reaches zero, the action still allows the request to proceed because it only checks its own remaining balance. The service layer then fails when it tries to consume the same token, but it returns early without throwing an error.
